boundary: Part A samples 6 sections and 10 group elements per prime, 180 trials in total; the invariance is a property of the construction rather than a sampled fact, but it is verified here and not derived.  Part B is EXHAUSTIVE over the 81 sections and the full group at q = 3.  Part C states a constraint and does not use it: no q = 5 invariant is proposed or tested.
headline: THE CHARACTERISTIC POLYNOMIAL IS A SYMPLECTIC INVARIANT, AND THE q = 3 MULTIPLICITIES ARE ORBIT SIZES.  Sp(2,p) acts on sections by (g . c)(v) = c(g^{-1} v) and charpoly(D) is constant on orbits -- 0 changes in 180 trials at p = 3, 5, 7.  At q = 3, Sp(2,3) has order 24 and acts on the 81 sections with SEVEN orbits of sizes 1, 8, 8, 8, 8, 24, 24; six characteristic polynomials occur, so exactly ONE coincidence happens -- two size-8 orbits share a polynomial, giving the class of 16.  So the multiplicities 1, 8, 8, 16, 24, 24 that Pass 535 left unexplained are orbit sizes with a single merge.  The merge itself is a genuine coincidence and is recorded, not explained.  Consequence for q = 5: whatever refines the valuation profile must itself be an Sp(2,5)-invariant.

part_A_symplectic_invariance.action: (g . c)(v) = c(g^{-1} v), for g in Sp(2,p)
part_A_symplectic_invariance.finding: charpoly(D) is constant on Sp(2,p)-orbits of sections; 0 changes in 180 trials across p = 3, 5, 7.

part_B_q3_orbit_structure.reading: SL(2,3) = Sp(2,3) has order 24 and acts on the 81 sections with SEVEN orbits of sizes 1, 8, 8, 8, 8, 24, 24.  Six characteristic polynomials occur, so exactly ONE coincidence happens: two of the four size-8 orbits share a polynomial, giving the class of size 16.  The multiplicities 1, 8, 8, 16, 24, 24 are therefore orbit sizes with a single merge -- not a numerical accident.
part_B_q3_orbit_structure.the_merge_is_unexplained: Two size-8 orbits are distinct as orbits and identical in characteristic polynomial.  No reason is offered; it is a coincidence of the same kind Pass 456 found for the q = 5 cospectral pair, and is recorded as one.

part_C_consequence_for_q5.not_used: Stated, not used.  No q = 5 invariant is proposed or tested here.
part_C_consequence_for_q5.sharper: More usefully: whatever refines the valuation profile at q = 5 -- the invariant Pass 524 showed must exist, since 34 profiles carry 52 trace vectors -- must itself be an Sp(2,5)-INVARIANT.  That is a real constraint on the search.
part_C_consequence_for_q5.statement: The image of the section space in charpoly space is a quotient of the ORBIT space, not of the section space.  At q = 5 that replaces 5^12 sections by at most 5^12/120 orbits.
